title: The lender logs every request and no response, so a provider throttle or outage cannot be seen from the host
foundBy: session agent operating two eight-member campaigns side by side on one host, reading every member's own CLI session records and the lender containers' logs after both campaigns had ended
details:
**What happened.** Two campaigns ran for hours at a provider's per-minute token ceiling, and half of one CLI family's turns were ended by it. The lender fronted every one of those calls. Its container log held a `lending` line for each: sandbox, slot, loan, method and path, more than two thousand lines across the two groups. It held **not one line recording what the upstream answered**: no status, no 429, no 5xx, no latency. The throttle was found hours later, by pulling each member's CLI session store out of its sandbox before destroy.

**Why.** `Server.ServeHTTP` in `internal/lend/proxy.go` logs at the moment it decides to lend, then hands the request to an `httputil.ReverseProxy` that has a `Rewrite` and an `ErrorHandler` and no `ModifyResponse`. The response passes through untouched, which is right for the body and means the status is never looked at. `Stats` counts requests, lent, refused, tunnels and blocked, and nothing about outcomes.

**Why it matters.** The lender is the one place on the host that sees every model call of every member of every group, for every provider it fronts. It is where *"is the provider refusing us?"* can be answered in one line, for any CLI, without reading a session format. Today a throttled key, a provider outage and a healthy quiet fleet produce the same log. An expired login already has this problem from the other side (SBX-030: the guest gets a bare 401 and nothing on the host says why).

**What is asked for.** Record the upstream's answer per request: status, duration, and for 429 and 503 the `Retry-After` and any rate-limit headers the provider sends. Record headers and status only, never a body. Count outcomes in `Stats` by slot and status class, so the summary line reads, for example, `openai: 1011 lent · 214 throttled · 0 5xx`. Warn, once per slot per interval, when a slot starts being throttled or starts failing, so that it is loud at the time and not discoverable afterwards. Keep the log somewhere that outlives the group: it lives in the lender container's own log now, and destroying the group takes it.

**How to reproduce the gap.** Create a sandbox with a lent key, and point the slot's origin at a stub that answers 429. Make a model call from the guest, and read the lender's log. It holds one `lending` line, identical to a success.

notes.text: The `details` text was copy-edited so the repository's prose gate passes: long sentences were split and em-dashes removed, and no claim was changed. The text as filed is in commit c059533.
